{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgPFKTci1cLmUp6neMaDB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT ARCHITECTURE.md ===\n# ARCHITECTURE: LayersTesting\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Module layout, boundaries, exit-code and output contracts for the `ledger` command-line cash ledger. |\n| Provides | ledger executable, bin/test.sh launcher contract |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`ledger` is a single command-line executable at the application root. It keeps accounts,\ncategories, and cash transactions in a relational database reached only through the shipped\npersistence library. Every command either completes in full or changes nothing. Balances never go\nbelow zero. Money is stored and computed as integer cents at every layer.\n\n## Technology Stack\n\nDerived from `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md`; it is the decision of record.\n\n| Technology | Where it applies |\n|------------|------------------|\n| Python 3.11+ | All application code, the `ledger` launcher, and the tests. |\n| SQLite | Default database, reached through the shipped persistence library. PostgreSQL is selected by DSN and goes through the same library. |\n| CLI foundation | The `cli` package and the `ledger` executable at the application root. |\n| pytest | The test runner behind `bin/test.sh`. |\n| POSIX sh | `bin/test.sh` and the supplied grader. |\n\n## Modules\n\n| Path | Responsibility |\n|------|----------------|\n| `ledger` | Executable launcher at the application root. Activates the environment, calls `cli.main(sys.argv[1:])`, exits with its return value. |\n| `cli/__init__.py` | `main(argv) -> int`: dispatch, exit-code mapping, CSV output, diagnostic line. |\n| `cli/errors.py` | `LedgerError` and its subclasses `OperationalError` (1), `UsageError` (2), `Rejected` (3), `NotFound` (4). |\n| `cli/registry.py` | `register(words, handler, nargs)`: the command table. |\n| `cli/config.py` | `resolve_dsn(environ)`: database location. |\n| `cli/context.py` | `open_store()`: opens the database through `persistence.open_database`. |\n| `cli/core.py` | Shared amount, text, date, and balance rules. |\n| `cli/commands/` | One module per command family. Each registers its handlers on import. |\n| `cli/testing.py` | `cli_runner(*args) -> (exit_code, stdout, stderr)`. |\n| `persistence/` | Shipped and generated by Drydock. Never hand-written. |\n| `bin/test.sh`, `tests/` | The application's own pytest suite and its POSIX launcher. |\n\n## Module Ownership\n\n| Boundary | Owner | Allowed low-level access |\n|----------|-------|--------------------------|\n| Persistence | `persistence/` package | The database drivers. Nothing else imports a driver. |\n| Configuration | `cli/config.py` | `os.environ` for `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_PATH`. |\n| File stores | `cli/commands/load_*.py` | Reads the CSV file named on the command line. Never reads anything under `sources/` by fixed path. |\n| External services | None | A PostgreSQL server only, and only through the persistence library. |\n\n## Command Flow\n\n1. `main` parses `argv`, finds the longest registered command prefix, and checks argument count.\n2. The handler checks every input and every rule, computes the full change, and only then writes.\n3. The handler returns rows (a header row and data rows) or `None`.\n4. `main` writes the rows to standard output as CSV only after the handler has returned.\n5. A raised `LedgerError` becomes its exit code and one line on standard error; standard output stays empty.\n\n## Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success. |\n| 1 | Operational failure: database unreachable, tables missing, file unreadable, or any unexpected exception. |\n| 2 | Usage error: unknown command, table, or report; wrong argument count. |\n| 3 | Rejected: invalid input, duplicate key, unknown reference, account in use, or a change that would leave a negative balance. |\n| 4 | Not found: an absent account or transaction id. |\n\n## Output Contract\n\nSuccessful commands except `init` write CSV: one header row, then data rows, comma-separated, no\nquoting, no trailing spaces, `\\n` line endings. Amounts print with exactly two decimals, a leading\n`-` when negative, and no thousands separator. Failures write nothing to standard output and one\ndiagnostic line to standard error.\n\n## Guardrails on Design\n\n- Report values, counts, and totals are always computed from database reads, never embedded.\n- No floating point for money at any layer.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or any seed file; seed files reach the database only through `ledger load`.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC arch-launcher ===\nIntent: The ledger launcher exists at the application root, is executable, and starts with an interpreter line.\n\nimport os\n\nassert os.path.isfile(\"ledger\")\nassert os.access(\"ledger\", os.X_OK)\nwith open(\"ledger\", \"rb\") as fh:\n    head = fh.read(2)\nassert head == b\"#!\"\n=== END AC arch-launcher ===\n\n=== AC arch-project-manifest ===\nIntent: The project declares a Python requirement in pyproject.toml and commits a uv.lock.\n\nimport os\nimport tomllib\n\nwith open(\"pyproject.toml\", \"rb\") as fh:\n    data = tomllib.load(fh)\nassert \"requires-python\" in data[\"project\"]\nassert os.path.isfile(\"uv.lock\")\n=== END AC arch-project-manifest ===\n\n=== AC arch-no-driver-imports ===\nIntent: No application file outside the persistence package imports a database driver.\n\nimport ast\nimport os\n\nforbidden = {\"sqlite3\", \"psycopg\", \"psycopg2\"}\nskip = {\".venv\", \"persistence\", \"sources\", \"tests\", \"__pycache__\", \".git\", \"blueprint\"}\noffenders = []\nfor root, dirs, files in os.walk(\".\"):\n    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in skip]\n    for name in files:\n        if not (name.endswith(\".py\") or name == \"ledger\"):\n            continue\n        path = os.path.join(root, name)\n        with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\n            src = fh.read()\n        try:\n            tree = ast.parse(src)\n        except SyntaxError:\n            continue\n        for node in ast.walk(tree):\n            if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n                mods = [a.name.split(\".\")[0] for a in node.names]\n            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):\n                mods = [(node.module or \"\").split(\".\")[0]]\n            else:\n                continue\n            offenders += [(path, m) for m in mods if m in forbidden]\nassert offenders == []\n=== END AC arch-no-driver-imports ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not modify, rewrite, regenerate, or substitute any file under `sources/`.\n- Do not open a database driver outside the shipped persistence library.\n- Do not use floating point for money at any layer.\n- Do not hardcode a report row, a count, or a total.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CliEntry.md ===\n# FEATURE: Cli Entry\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The cli package entry point: command registry, dispatch, exit-code mapping, CSV output, diagnostics, and database location. |\n| Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE.md |\n| Provides | cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, cli.registry.register, cli.errors, cli.config.resolve_dsn, cli.context.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command in the ledger plugs into one dispatcher. This story builds the dispatcher and registers no command. Later stories add modules under `cli/commands/` that call `register`. `main` imports every module in the `cli.commands` package (for example with `pkgutil.iter_modules`) before dispatching, so adding a command never edits `main`.\n\n## Interface\n\n| Symbol | Contract |\n|--------|----------|\n| `cli.main(argv=None) -> int` | Runs one command and returns its exit code. `None` means `sys.argv[1:]`. |\n| `cli.registry.register(words, handler, nargs)` | `words` is a tuple such as `(\"account\", \"add\")`. `handler(args: list[str])` returns a list of rows (each a list of strings) or `None`. `nargs` is `(min, max)` for the arguments after the words. |\n| `cli.errors.LedgerError(message)` | Base class with an integer `code`. Subclasses: `OperationalError` 1, `UsageError` 2, `Rejected` 3, `NotFound` 4. |\n| `cli.config.resolve_dsn(environ) -> str` | Returns `DATABASE_URL`, else `DATABASE_PATH`, else the absolute path of `data/app.db` under the application root. An empty value counts as unset. The value is returned as written; the persistence library selects the engine and strips an optional `sqlite://` prefix. |\n| `cli.context.open_store()` | Calls `persistence.open_database(resolve_dsn(os.environ))`. For a SQLite file it creates a missing parent directory first. |\n| `cli.testing.cli_runner(*args)` | Returns `(exit_code, stdout, stderr)` by calling `main` in process. |\n\n## Dispatch Rules\n\n- The longest registered word prefix of `argv` selects the handler. No match, or no arguments at all, is a usage error (exit 2).\n- An argument count outside `nargs` is a usage error (exit 2) and the handler is not called.\n- The handler runs to completion before anything is written to standard output. Rows are then written with `csv.writer` semantics but unquoted fields, `\\n` line endings, and `sys.stdout` looked up at call time.\n- A `LedgerError` becomes its `code`, one diagnostic line on standard error, and nothing on standard output.\n- A `persistence.PersistenceError` and any other unexpected exception become exit 1 with one diagnostic line.\n- Diagnostics are never part of any contract; only the exit code and standard output are.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned by DATABASE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC cli-unknown-command ===\nIntent: An unknown command exits 2 with nothing on standard output and one diagnostic line.\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-no-such-command\")\nprint(out, err)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC cli-unknown-command ===\n\n=== AC cli-no-arguments ===\nIntent: Running with no arguments is a usage error.\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner()\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-no-arguments ===\n\n=== AC cli-success-csv ===\nIntent: A registered handler's rows are written as unquoted CSV with LF endings and exit 0.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\n\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nrows = [[\"h1\", \"h2\"], [\"v1\", \"v2\"]]\nregister((\"zz-accept-ok\",), lambda args: rows, (0, 0))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-accept-ok\")\nassert code == 0\nassert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out, newline=\"\"))) == rows\nassert \"\\r\" not in out\nassert out.endswith(\"\\n\")\n=== END AC cli-success-csv ===\n\n=== AC cli-no-output-handler ===\nIntent: A handler returning None exits 0 and writes nothing to standard output.\n\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nregister((\"zz-accept-quiet\",), lambda args: None, (0, 0))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-accept-quiet\")\nassert code == 0\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-no-output-handler ===\n\n=== AC cli-error-codes ===\nIntent: Each LedgerError subclass maps to its exit code and an unexpected exception maps to 1, with empty standard output.\n\nfrom cli.errors import NotFound, OperationalError, Rejected, UsageError\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncases = {\n    \"zz-rej\": (Rejected, 3),\n    \"zz-nf\": (NotFound, 4),\n    \"zz-op\": (OperationalError, 1),\n    \"zz-us\": (UsageError, 2),\n}\nfor name, (exc, want) in cases.items():\n    def handler(args, exc=exc):\n        raise exc(\"diagnostic\")\n    register((name,), handler, (0, 0))\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(name)\n    print(name, code, err)\n    assert code == want\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n\ndef boom(args):\n    raise RuntimeError(\"unexpected\")\n\nregister((\"zz-boom\",), boom, (0, 0))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-boom\")\nassert code == 1\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-error-codes ===\n\n=== AC cli-argument-count ===\nIntent: Too few or too many arguments is exit 2 and the handler runs only for a count within range.\n\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncalls = []\n\ndef handler(args):\n    calls.append(list(args))\n    return [[\"x\"]]\n\nregister((\"zz-one\",), handler, (1, 1))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-one\")\nassert code == 2\nassert calls == []\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-one\", \"a\", \"b\")\nassert code == 2\nassert calls == []\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-one\", \"a\")\nassert code == 0\nassert calls == [[\"a\"]]\n=== END AC cli-argument-count ===\n\n=== AC cli-multiword-command ===\nIntent: A two-word command dispatches on both words; the first word alone or an unknown second word is exit 2.\n\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nregister((\"zz-grp\", \"sub\"), lambda args: [[\"ok\"]], (0, 0))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-grp\", \"sub\")\nassert code == 0\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-grp\")\nassert code == 2\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-grp\", \"nosuch\")\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-multiword-command ===\n\n=== AC cli-resolve-dsn ===\nIntent: The database location resolves from DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db.\n\nfrom cli.config import resolve_dsn\n\nurl = \"postgresql://example.invalid/ledger\"\npath = \"custom/ledger.db\"\nassert resolve_dsn({\"DATABASE_URL\": url, \"DATABASE_PATH\": path}) == url\nassert resolve_dsn({\"DATABASE_PATH\": path}) == path\nassert resolve_dsn({\"DATABASE_URL\": \"\", \"DATABASE_PATH\": path}) == path\ndefault = resolve_dsn({})\nassert default.endswith(\"app.db\")\n=== END AC cli-resolve-dsn ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Nothing is written to standard output until the handler has returned successfully.\n- Diagnostics go to standard error and are never compared.\n- This story registers no command.\n- Application code never imports a database driver; it uses `persistence.open_database`.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LedgerCore.md ===\n# FEATURE: Ledger Core\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Shared integer-cent amount parsing and formatting, field and date validators, and the projected-balance guard. |\n| Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE.md, FEATURE-CliEntry.md |\n| Provides | cli.core.parse_amount, cli.core.format_amount, cli.core.validate_code, cli.core.validate_text, cli.core.validate_name, cli.core.validate_memo, cli.core.validate_date, cli.core.account_balance, cli.core.balance_guard |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command shares the same input rules. They live in `cli/core.py` so that no command repeats or contradicts them. All validators raise `cli.errors.Rejected` (exit 3) and perform no database write.\n\n## Rules\n\n| Function | Contract |\n|----------|----------|\n| `parse_amount(text) -> int` | Accepts only ASCII text matching `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`. Returns integer cents using integer arithmetic only. Zero (such as `0`, `0.00`, `-0.0`) is rejected. More than two decimals, a missing integer part, a plus sign, spaces, or a thousands separator is rejected. |\n| `format_amount(cents) -> str` | Exactly two decimals, a leading `-` when negative, no thousands separator. `0` prints as the zero amount with two decimals. |\n| `validate_code(text) -> str` | 1 to 12 characters from `A-Z` and `0-9`. |\n| `validate_text(text, min_len, max_len) -> str` | Length within bounds; no comma, `\\n`, or `\\r`. |\n| `validate_name(text)` | `validate_text` with 1 to 40 characters. Used for account names and category descriptions. |\n| `validate_memo(text)` | `validate_text` with 0 to 60 characters. |\n| `validate_date(text) -> str` | Matches `YYYY-MM-DD` with four-digit year, two-digit month and day, and is a real calendar date. A date such as the thirtieth of February is rejected. |\n| `account_balance(db, account) -> int` | Sum of the account's transaction amounts, read with `db.transactions.list(account=...)`. Zero when it has none. |\n| `balance_guard(db, deltas) -> None` | `deltas` maps account code to a net change in cents. Computes each account's balance after applying its delta and raises `Rejected` when any resulting balance is below zero. It never writes. |\n\nCommands call `balance_guard` with the full change set before their first write. A load passes the summed delta per account for the whole file; a transfer passes both accounts; amend passes the new amount minus the old; delete passes the negated old amount.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- `FEATURE-TXN-002` — read: list transactions to compute balances - returns: `amount`\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC core-parse-amount ===\nIntent: parse_amount converts valid decimal text to integer cents.\n\nfrom cli.core import parse_amount\n\nassert parse_amount(\"12.50\") == 1250\nassert parse_amount(\"-12.50\") == -1250\nassert parse_amount(\"5\") == 500\nassert parse_amount(\"7.5\") == 750\nassert parse_amount(\"0.01\") == 1\nassert parse_amount(\"5000.00\") == 500000\nassert isinstance(parse_amount(\"1.25\"), int)\n=== END AC core-parse-amount ===\n\n=== AC core-parse-amount-rejects ===\nIntent: parse_amount rejects zero, excess decimals, and malformed text with Rejected.\n\nfrom cli.core import parse_amount\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        parse_amount(text)\n    except Rejected:\n        return True\n    return False\n\nfor bad in [\"0\", \"0.00\", \"-0.0\", \"1.234\", \"\", \".5\", \"1.\", \"abc\", \"+1.00\", \"1,000.00\", \"1 .00\", \"--1\"]:\n    assert rejected(bad), bad\n=== END AC core-parse-amount-rejects ===\n\n=== AC core-format-amount ===\nIntent: format_amount prints two decimals, a leading minus when negative, and no thousands separator.\n\nfrom cli.core import format_amount, parse_amount\n\nassert format_amount(-1250) == \"-12.50\"\nassert format_amount(0) == \"0.00\"\nassert format_amount(500000) == \"5000.00\"\nassert format_amount(5) == \"0.05\"\nassert \",\" not in format_amount(123456789)\nfor cents in [1, -1, 99, 100, -100, 123456, -987654, 500000]:\n    assert parse_amount(format_amount(cents)) == cents\n=== END AC core-format-amount ===\n\n=== AC core-validate-code ===\nIntent: validate_code accepts 1 to 12 characters of A-Z and 0-9 and rejects everything else.\n\nfrom cli.core import validate_code\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\ngood = \"A\" * 12\nassert validate_code(good) == good\nassert validate_code(\"DRAWER1\") == \"DRAWER1\"\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        validate_code(text)\n    except Rejected:\n        return True\n    return False\n\nfor bad in [\"\", \"A\" * 13, \"drawer\", \"AB-C\", \"A B\", \"A,B\", \"ÅB\"]:\n    assert rejected(bad), bad\n=== END AC core-validate-code ===\n\n=== AC core-validate-text ===\nIntent: Names and memos enforce their length bounds and forbid comma and newline.\n\nfrom cli.core import validate_memo, validate_name\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\ndef rejected(fn, text):\n    try:\n        fn(text)\n    except Rejected:\n        return True\n    return False\n\nname40 = \"n\" * 40\nmemo60 = \"m\" * 60\nassert validate_name(name40) == name40\nassert validate_memo(memo60) == memo60\nassert validate_memo(\"\") == \"\"\nassert rejected(validate_name, \"\")\nassert rejected(validate_name, \"n\" * 41)\nassert rejected(validate_memo, \"m\" * 61)\nfor bad in [\"a,b\", \"a\\nb\", \"a\\rb\"]:\n    assert rejected(validate_name, bad)\n    assert rejected(validate_memo, bad)\n=== END AC core-validate-text ===\n\n=== AC core-validate-date ===\nIntent: validate_date accepts real YYYY-MM-DD dates and rejects impossible or malformed ones.\n\nfrom cli.core import validate_date\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        validate_date(text)\n    except Rejected:\n        return True\n    return False\n\nfor good in [\"2026-04-01\", \"2028-02-29\", \"2026-12-31\"]:\n    assert validate_date(good) == good\nfor bad in [\"2026-02-30\", \"2026-13-01\", \"2027-02-29\", \"2026-4-1\", \"20260401\", \"2026/04/01\", \"\", \"2026-04-01x\"]:\n    assert rejected(bad), bad\n=== END AC core-validate-date ===\n\n=== AC core-balance-guard ===\nIntent: balance_guard accepts a change that keeps every balance at or above zero, rejects one that goes below, and writes nothing.\n\nfrom cli.core import account_balance, balance_guard\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\nwith db_session() as db:\n    acct = \"ACPTBG1\"\n    cat = \"ACPTBGC\"\n    db.accounts.create(account=acct, name=\"Guard Account\")\n    db.categories.create(category=cat, description=\"Guard Category\")\n    new_id = max([t.txn_id for t in db.transactions.list()], default=0) + 1\n    funded = 1000\n    db.transactions.create(\n        txn_id=new_id, date=\"2026-06-01\", account=acct, category=cat, amount=funded, memo=\"\"\n    )\n    rows_before = len(db.transactions.list(account=acct))\n    assert account_balance(db, acct) == funded\n    balance_guard(db, {acct: -funded})\n    try:\n        balance_guard(db, {acct: -funded - 1})\n        raised = False\n    except Rejected:\n        raised = True\n    assert raised\n    assert len(db.transactions.list(account=acct)) == BEGIN ARTIFACT ARCHITECTURE.md ===\n# ARCHITECTURE: LayersTesting\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Module layout, boundaries, exit-code and output contracts for the `ledger` command-line cash ledger. |\n| Provides | ledger executable, bin/test.sh launcher contract |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`ledger` is a single command-line executable at the application root. It keeps accounts,\ncategories, and cash transactions in a relational database reached only through the shipped\npersistence library. Every command either completes in full or changes nothing. Balances never go\nbelow zero. Money is stored and computed as integer cents at every layer.\n\n## Technology Stack\n\nDerived from `TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md`; it is the decision of record.\n\n| Technology | Where it applies |\n|------------|------------------|\n| Python 3.11+ | All application code, the `ledger` launcher, and the tests. |\n| SQLite | Default database, reached through the shipped persistence library. PostgreSQL is selected by DSN and goes through the same library. |\n| CLI foundation | The `cli` package and the `ledger` executable at the application root. |\n| pytest | The test runner behind `bin/test.sh`. |\n| POSIX sh | `bin/test.sh` and the supplied grader. |\n\n## Modules\n\n| Path | Responsibility |\n|------|----------------|\n| `ledger` | Executable launcher at the application root. Activates the environment, calls `cli.main(sys.argv[1:])`, exits with its return value. |\n| `cli/__init__.py` | `main(argv) -> int`: dispatch, exit-code mapping, CSV output, diagnostic line. |\n| `cli/errors.py` | `LedgerError` and its subclasses `OperationalError` (1), `UsageError` (2), `Rejected` (3), `NotFound` (4). |\n| `cli/registry.py` | `register(words, handler, nargs)`: the command table. |\n| `cli/config.py` | `resolve_dsn(environ)`: database location. |\n| `cli/context.py` | `open_store()`: opens the database through `persistence.open_database`. |\n| `cli/core.py` | Shared amount, text, date, and balance rules. |\n| `cli/commands/` | One module per command family. Each registers its handlers on import. |\n| `cli/testing.py` | `cli_runner(*args) -> (exit_code, stdout, stderr)`. |\n| `persistence/` | Shipped and generated by Drydock. Never hand-written. |\n| `bin/test.sh`, `tests/` | The application's own pytest suite and its POSIX launcher. |\n\n## Module Ownership\n\n| Boundary | Owner | Allowed low-level access |\n|----------|-------|--------------------------|\n| Persistence | `persistence/` package | The database drivers. Nothing else imports a driver. |\n| Configuration | `cli/config.py` | `os.environ` for `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_PATH`. |\n| File stores | `cli/commands/load_*.py` | Reads the CSV file named on the command line. Never reads anything under `sources/` by fixed path. |\n| External services | None | A PostgreSQL server only, and only through the persistence library. |\n\n## Command Flow\n\n1. `main` parses `argv`, finds the longest registered command prefix, and checks argument count.\n2. The handler checks every input and every rule, computes the full change, and only then writes.\n3. The handler returns rows (a header row and data rows) or `None`.\n4. `main` writes the rows to standard output as CSV only after the handler has returned.\n5. A raised `LedgerError` becomes its exit code and one line on standard error; standard output stays empty.\n\n## Exit Codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| 0 | Success. |\n| 1 | Operational failure: database unreachable, tables missing, file unreadable, or any unexpected exception. |\n| 2 | Usage error: unknown command, table, or report; wrong argument count. |\n| 3 | Rejected: invalid input, duplicate key, unknown reference, account in use, or a change that would leave a negative balance. |\n| 4 | Not found: an absent account or transaction id. |\n\n## Output Contract\n\nSuccessful commands except `init` write CSV: one header row, then data rows, comma-separated, no\nquoting, no trailing spaces, `\\n` line endings. Amounts print with exactly two decimals, a leading\n`-` when negative, and no thousands separator. Failures write nothing to standard output and one\ndiagnostic line to standard error.\n\n## Guardrails on Design\n\n- Report values, counts, and totals are always computed from database reads, never embedded.\n- No floating point for money at any layer.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or any seed file; seed files reach the database only through `ledger load`.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC arch-launcher ===\nIntent: The ledger launcher exists at the application root, is executable, and starts with an interpreter line.\n\nimport os\n\nassert os.path.isfile(\"ledger\")\nassert os.access(\"ledger\", os.X_OK)\nwith open(\"ledger\", \"rb\") as fh:\n    head = fh.read(2)\nassert head == b\"#!\"\n=== END AC arch-launcher ===\n\n=== AC arch-project-manifest ===\nIntent: The project declares a Python requirement in pyproject.toml and commits a uv.lock.\n\nimport os\nimport tomllib\n\nwith open(\"pyproject.toml\", \"rb\") as fh:\n    data = tomllib.load(fh)\nassert \"requires-python\" in data[\"project\"]\nassert os.path.isfile(\"uv.lock\")\n=== END AC arch-project-manifest ===\n\n=== AC arch-no-driver-imports ===\nIntent: No application file outside the persistence package imports a database driver.\n\nimport ast\nimport os\n\nforbidden = {\"sqlite3\", \"psycopg\", \"psycopg2\"}\nskip = {\".venv\", \"persistence\", \"sources\", \"tests\", \"__pycache__\", \".git\", \"blueprint\"}\noffenders = []\nfor root, dirs, files in os.walk(\".\"):\n    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in skip]\n    for name in files:\n        if not (name.endswith(\".py\") or name == \"ledger\"):\n            continue\n        path = os.path.join(root, name)\n        with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\n            src = fh.read()\n        try:\n            tree = ast.parse(src)\n        except SyntaxError:\n            continue\n        for node in ast.walk(tree):\n            if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n                mods = [a.name.split(\".\")[0] for a in node.names]\n            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):\n                mods = [(node.module or \"\").split(\".\")[0]]\n            else:\n                continue\n            offenders += [(path, m) for m in mods if m in forbidden]\nassert offenders == []\n=== END AC arch-no-driver-imports ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Do not modify, rewrite, regenerate, or substitute any file under `sources/`.\n- Do not open a database driver outside the shipped persistence library.\n- Do not use floating point for money at any layer.\n- Do not hardcode a report row, a count, or a total.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CliEntry.md ===\n# FEATURE: Cli Entry\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | The cli package entry point: command registry, dispatch, exit-code mapping, CSV output, diagnostics, and database location. |\n| Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE.md |\n| Provides | cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, cli.registry.register, cli.errors, cli.config.resolve_dsn, cli.context.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery command in the ledger plugs into one dispatcher. This story builds the dispatcher and registers no command. Later stories add modules under `cli/commands/` that call `register`. `main` imports every module in the `cli.commands` package (for example with `pkgutil.iter_modules`) before dispatching, so adding a command never edits `main`.\n\n## Interface\n\n| Symbol | Contract |\n|--------|----------|\n| `cli.main(argv=None) -> int` | Runs one command and returns its exit code. `None` means `sys.argv[1:]`. |\n| `cli.registry.register(words, handler, nargs)` | `words` is a tuple such as `(\"account\", \"add\")`. `handler(args: list[str])` returns a list of rows (each a list of strings) or `None`. `nargs` is `(min, max)` for the arguments after the words. |\n| `cli.errors.LedgerError(message)` | Base class with an integer `code`. Subclasses: `OperationalError` 1, `UsageError` 2, `Rejected` 3, `NotFound` 4. |\n| `cli.config.resolve_dsn(environ) -> str` | Returns `DATABASE_URL`, else `DATABASE_PATH`, else the absolute path of `data/app.db` under the application root. An empty value counts as unset. The value is returned as written; the persistence library selects the engine and strips an optional `sqlite://` prefix. |\n| `cli.context.open_store()` | Calls `persistence.open_database(resolve_dsn(os.environ))`. For a SQLite file it creates a missing parent directory first. |\n| `cli.testing.cli_runner(*args)` | Returns `(exit_code, stdout, stderr)` by calling `main` in process. |\n\n## Dispatch Rules\n\n- The longest registered word prefix of `argv` selects the handler. No match, or no arguments at all, is a usage error (exit 2).\n- An argument count outside `nargs` is a usage error (exit 2) and the handler is not called.\n- The handler runs to completion before anything is written to standard output. Rows are then written with `csv.writer` semantics but unquoted fields, `\\n` line endings, and `sys.stdout` looked up at call time.\n- A `LedgerError` becomes its `code`, one diagnostic line on standard error, and nothing on standard output.\n- A `persistence.PersistenceError` and any other unexpected exception become exit 1 with one diagnostic line.\n- Diagnostics are never part of any contract; only the exit code and standard output are.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned by DATABASE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC cli-unknown-command ===\nIntent: An unknown command exits 2 with nothing on standard output and one diagnostic line.\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-no-such-command\")\nprint(out, err)\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\nassert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC cli-unknown-command ===\n\n=== AC cli-no-arguments ===\nIntent: Running with no arguments is a usage error.\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\ncode, out, err = cli_runner()\nassert code == 2\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-no-arguments ===\n\n=== AC cli-success-csv ===\nIntent: A registered handler's rows are written as unquoted CSV with LF endings and exit 0.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\n\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nrows = [[\"h1\", \"h2\"], [\"v1\", \"v2\"]]\nregister((\"zz-accept-ok\",), lambda args: rows, (0, 0))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-accept-ok\")\nassert code == 0\nassert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out, newline=\"\"))) == rows\nassert \"\\r\" not in out\nassert out.endswith(\"\\n\")\n=== END AC cli-success-csv ===\n\n=== AC cli-no-output-handler ===\nIntent: A handler returning None exits 0 and writes nothing to standard output.\n\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nregister((\"zz-accept-quiet\",), lambda args: None, (0, 0))\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"zz-accept-quiet\")\nassert code == 0\nassert out == \"\"\n=== END AC cli-no-output-handler ===\n\n=== AC cli-error-codes ===\nIntent: Each LedgerError subclass maps to its exit code and an unexpected exception maps to 1, with empty standard output.\n\nfrom cli.errors import NotFound, OperationalError, Rejected, UsageError\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.testing import FEATURE-CliEntry.md, FEATURE-LedgerCore.md |\n| Provides | ledger init |\n| Consumes | cli.registry.register, cli.context.open_store |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`ledger init` drops all three tables if present and recreates them empty, writing nothing to standard output. It takes no arguments; any argument is a usage error (exit 2) and changes nothing. This is the contract surfaced in the commands table of the source instructions.\n\n## Behavior\n\n1. Open the store with `cli.context.open_store()`.\n2. Make sure the three tables exist. If opening a store that has no tables does not already create them, apply the generated idempotent `schema.sql` through the persistence library's own facility. Application code never executes driver calls itself. The grader runs `ledger init` against a brand-new database file, so this step must work on an empty store.\n3. Empty the tables in foreign-key order with the declared clear operations: transactions first, then accounts, then categories.\n4. Return `None` so standard output stays empty; exit 0.\n5. An unreachable database exits 1.\n\nThe registration is `register((\"init\",), handler, (0, 0))` in `cli/commands/init.py`.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- `FEATURE-ACCOUNT-006` — write: remove every
